original_claim_summary: The United States allegedly blocked multiple U.N. Gaza ceasefire resolutions beginning in October 2023, a period that includes Biden administration decisions.

source_urls.access_notes: UN report text retrieved; describes the June 4, 2025 Council vote.
supports: On June 4, 2025, the United States vetoed a draft resolution demanding an immediate and permanent Gaza ceasefire.
The other 14 Security Council members voted in favor; the U.S. cast the lone vote against.

source_urls.publisher: United Nations Security Council meeting coverage
supports: The Council failed to adopt the resolution owing to the U.S. veto, despite the other 14 affirmative votes.

supported_facts: A discrete Trump-administration veto occurred on June 4, 2025, on a draft resolution calling for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza.
The resolution failed after the U.S. veto; 14 other Council members voted for it.
unsupported_original_claims: The June 2025 source does not support attributing the October 2023 vetoes to Trump; Trump was not president then.
The cited source establishes one June 2025 veto, not a series of multiple vetoes by the Trump administration.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: United States vetoes Gaza ceasefire resolution at UN Security Council
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: On June 4, 2025, the United States vetoed a draft U.N. Security Council resolution calling for an immediate, unconditional, permanent ceasefire in Gaza; the other 14 Council members voted in favor.

exact_evidence_gap: The supplied title spans vetoes beginning in October 2023, but the evidence reviewed verifies only the June 4, 2025 Trump-era vote and cannot attribute earlier votes to Trump.
disposition_rationale: Limit this entry to the one verified Trump-era veto and separate any earlier Biden-era votes into their own sourced events.

original_claim_summary: Trump allegedly said in 2018 that he knew more about nuclear weapons than anyone.

source_urls.access_notes: Exact campaign-speech transcript linked in the packet and reviewed for date, setting and wording.
supports: Trump made the nuclear-knowledge boast at an April 2, 2016 campaign appearance in Eau Claire, Wisconsin.
The recorded wording compares his knowledge with Barack Obama's: 'I know more about nuclear than he'll ever know.'

supported_facts: The boast is documented in the Eau Claire transcript dated April 2, 2016.
The comparison was to Obama, not to 'anyone.'
unsupported_original_claims: 2018 is not the date shown in the transcript.
The source does not record the wording 'more than anyone'; it names Obama as the comparison target.
The statement is a campaign boast, not evidence that Trump had superior nuclear expertise.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: Trump boasts about nuclear knowledge compared with Obama at 2016 rally
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: At an April 2, 2016 campaign appearance in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, Donald Trump said, 'I know more about nuclear than he'll ever know,' referring to President Barack Obama. The transcript documents the remark, not the truth of the boast.

exact_evidence_gap: No source reviewed supports the 2018 date or the 'more than anyone' wording; the transcript directly identifies a different year and comparison target.
disposition_rationale: Correct the date and exact comparison while presenting the quote as an attributed campaign statement.

original_claim_summary: Trump allegedly knew in advance, through Roger Stone's texts, about WikiLeaks' October 7, 2016 release of John Podesta's emails.

source_urls.publisher: U.S. Government Publishing Office / Special Counsel Robert Mueller
source_urls.access_notes: Official report landing page and report text reviewed; relevant account is in Volume I's WikiLeaks discussion.
supports: The report describes Stone claiming knowledge of future WikiLeaks releases and communications between Stone and campaign associates about WikiLeaks.
It documents campaign contacts and statements, but does not establish that Trump was told in advance of the specific October 7 Podesta email release.

source_urls.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Special Counsel's Office
source_urls.access_notes: Official Mueller report PDF; use the report's own account rather than later characterizations of the texts.
supports: The report summarizes what witnesses said about Stone and campaign contacts concerning WikiLeaks; it does not conclude that Trump had advance knowledge of the specific Podesta release.

supported_facts: Mueller's report recounts that Stone claimed to have advance knowledge of future WikiLeaks releases and had campaign contacts concerning WikiLeaks.
The report did not establish the specific claim that Trump knew before WikiLeaks began publishing Podesta emails on October 7, 2016.
unsupported_original_claims: The report does not state that Stone's texts prove Trump knew in advance of the specific October 7 release.
Evidence that Stone discussed WikiLeaks with campaign figures is not proof that the information reached Trump or established the date/content of the release.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: Mueller report documents Stone's WikiLeaks claims and campaign contacts
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: The Mueller report describes Roger Stone's claims about future WikiLeaks releases and his contacts with Trump campaign associates. It does not establish that Donald Trump knew in advance of WikiLeaks' specific October 7, 2016 release of John Podesta's emails.

exact_evidence_gap: The report does not establish a communication that conveyed the specific October 7 release to Trump before publication; the claimed inference from Stone's contacts to Trump's advance knowledge is unsupported.
disposition_rationale: Retain the report's documented Stone/campaign contacts, but do not convert them into a finding of advance presidential knowledge.

original_claim_summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio allegedly purged more than 1,300 career diplomats in February 2025.

source_urls.access_notes: Reuters article text retrieved; it reports July 11 notices for U.S.-based employees.
supports: The State Department began firing 1,353 U.S.-based employees on July 11, 2025.
The announced breakdown was 1,107 civil-service employees and 246 Foreign Service officers.

source_urls.access_notes: AP report excerpt retrieved; confirms the layoff notices and domestic assignment scope.
supports: The department sent notices to 1,107 civil servants and 246 Foreign Service officers with assignments in the United States.

supported_facts: A July 11, 2025 State Department reduction affected 1,353 U.S.-based employees: 1,107 civil-service and 246 Foreign Service employees.
The report describes U.S.-based Foreign Service officers and civil servants, not solely career diplomats posted abroad.
unsupported_original_claims: The event date was July 11, 2025, not February.
The 1,353 total includes civil-service employees and Foreign Service officers, not 1,353 career diplomats.
The report does not establish that Rubio personally purged all career diplomats or all State Department diplomats.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: State Department begins July 2025 layoffs affecting 1,353 U.S.-based employees
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: On July 11, 2025, the State Department began a reduction in force affecting 1,353 U.S.-based employees: 1,107 civil servants and 246 Foreign Service officers. The number does not represent all career diplomats or diplomats posted overseas.

exact_evidence_gap: The original February date and characterization as a purge of 1,300-plus career diplomats are not supported by the July layoff reporting.
disposition_rationale: Correct the month and describe the affected employee groups using the reported breakdown.

original_claim_summary: DOGE allegedly fired about 10,000 USAID workers and contractors and ended all U.S. foreign aid programs.

source_urls.source_type: news reporting based on sources familiar with the plan
source_urls.access_notes: Reuters article text retrieved; the initial staff count was a reported plan, not a final audited separation total.
supports: On February 6, Reuters reported a plan to retain 294 of USAID's more than 10,000 worldwide staff.
The article reports some staff placed on leave, contractors laid off, and programs left in limbo; it does not say every worker had already been fired.

source_urls.source_type: news reporting with attributed Secretary of State statement
source_urls.access_notes: Reuters report text retrieved; the 83% figure is attributed to Rubio's public statement.
supports: On March 10, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration had canceled more than 80% of USAID programs after a six-week review, and that remaining programs would be administered by the State Department.

supported_facts: Reuters reported a February plan to reduce USAID's worldwide staff to 294 from more than 10,000; this was a reported plan and included leave/contractor actions, not a verified 10,000 completed firings.
Rubio said in March that more than 80% of USAID programs had been canceled and that roughly 1,000 remaining programs would move under State Department administration.
unsupported_original_claims: The sources do not establish that DOGE fired all approximately 10,000 USAID employees and contractors; the 294 figure was a reported planned retained workforce, and the reports distinguish staff from contractors and foreign-national employees.
Cancellation of over 80% of USAID programs does not mean all U.S. foreign aid ended; Reuters says remaining programs were to be administered by State.
The sources do not support treating Rubio's 83% figure as an independently audited count; it is his attributed announcement.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: Trump administration plans deep USAID staffing cuts and cancels over 80% of programs
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: Reuters reported in February 2025 that the administration planned to retain 294 of USAID's more than 10,000 worldwide staff. In March, Rubio said it had canceled more than 80% of USAID programs, with remaining programs moving to the State Department. These reports do not establish that all 10,000 workers were fired or that all U.S. foreign aid ended.

exact_evidence_gap: The sources do not provide a final, comprehensive staff separation count or support the claim that every U.S. foreign-aid program ended; the staffing number was a plan and the program-cancellation figure was attributed to Rubio.
disposition_rationale: Attribute the reported plan and announced program cancellations, distinguish employees from contractors, and avoid claiming that all personnel or aid were eliminated.
